nodes.label: Decision 001 — Language: Python
nodes.rationale: HMM ecosystem (hmmlearn), pandas, FastAPI, Kite/Delta SDKs are all native to Python and the user is already proficient; adding a second runtime buys nothing. Commits the project to a single toolchain with type hints and pydantic DTOs.

nodes.label: Decision 002 — Hosting: Railway (not AWS)
nodes.rationale: For a solo 24/7 workload at Rs50k starting capital, Railway's near-zero DevOps overhead beats AWS; AWS only wins at a scale this project will not reach. Accepts per-service resource caps; revisit only for multi-region or sub-100ms execution.

nodes.label: Decision 003 — Dashboard: FastAPI + HTMX single service
nodes.rationale: Server-rendered HTML halves the Railway service count and removes the Node toolchain for a solo user with no SaaS aspirations; HTMX polling/SSE suffices for live updates. Rules out SPA features.

nodes.label: Decision 004 — Binance signals, Delta India execution
nodes.rationale: Binance has the highest global crypto volume so gives best price discovery, while Delta India is the Indian-resident-friendly execution venue. Forces a symbol mapping table (BTCUSDT to BTCUSD), Delta funding rate and Delta order-book depth for logic, a price-drift monitor with auto-pause, and a re-evaluation at 5-15M timeframes where 150-250ms latency may exceed the edge.

nodes.label: Decision 005 — Stocks via Zerodha Kite Connect (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Assumed Kite was the only legal route for live NSE data plus an existing user system on Kite. Superseded by 012 when it turned out that existing system did not exist.

nodes.label: Decision 006 — Strategy params: YAML in git, not DB
nodes.rationale: Reversibility, diffability and forced deliberation — mutable runtime config is how people lose money at 3am. Consequences: dashboard is read-only for params, bad YAML fails the bot fast, and an LLM tuner may only open a PR.

nodes.label: Decision 007 — Postgres truth + nightly Google Drive mirror
nodes.rationale: Cloud-primary survives laptop loss while the local Drive mirror gives offline access and backtester-friendly Parquet. CSV is for human review, Parquet for backtester ingest.

nodes.label: Decision 008 — Deterministic core, agentic perimeter
nodes.rationale: Determinism buys backtest parity, sub-second latency, low cost, auditable decisions and regulatory defensibility. LLM agents may only read the DB and write reports or open PRs; they never touch order placement.

nodes.label: Decision 009 — Backtest engine out of scope for this repo
nodes.rationale: User preference keeps the live-trading repo small and focused; strategy logic is exposed as importable modules so the backtester consumes it without duplication. Forces strategy modules to avoid live-only top-level imports so data and broker can be swapped.

nodes.label: Decision 010 — Alerts via Telegram
nodes.rationale: Free, reliable in India, mobile-first. The alert module no-ops when the env vars are unset so a testnet run without Telegram still works.

nodes.label: Decision 011 — Session continuity: CLAUDE.md + PHASES.md + DECISIONS.md
nodes.rationale: The user wants to resume work in new sessions without re-briefing, so decisions are written to disk rather than living in chat memory. Every session ends by ticking PHASES.md and committing.

nodes.label: Decision 012 — Stocks broker: switch Zerodha to Dhan
nodes.rationale: Decision 005 assumed an existing live Kite system that does not exist; Dhan has a free API tier vs Rs2k/month, longer-lived tokens, and the user already holds an account. Removes all Kite config/adapter code and swaps the BrokerName enum ZERODHA to DHAN.

nodes.label: Decision 013 — Six (type x market) buckets with isolated capital
nodes.rationale: Matches the user's PPTX instructions and Goal_Setting.txt percentages; isolation means a blowup in one strategy class cannot drain another and per-bucket sizing simplifies Kelly accounting. Cross-bucket rebalancing is explicitly out of scope for v1 and Indian buckets ship disabled until the Dhan adapter lands.

nodes.label: Decision 014 — Per-bucket regime HMM at the bucket's timeframe
nodes.rationale: Regime timeframe must match strategy timeframe rather than one global regime; three states are robust to limited crypto history while 5-state Crash/Euphoria is deferred until 3+ months of live signal. Models are stored as JSONB hmmlearn params in Postgres — no pickle, no filesystem.

nodes.label: Decision 015 — Kelly on bucket capital with insufficient-balance skip
nodes.rationale: Skipping under-sized trades entirely preserves Kelly's edge profile — partial fills change the variance of returns and ruin optimality. Backtester-fed per-symbol mu/sigma with a backtest_ref keeps param choices auditable; live rolling estimation deferred to Phase 7.

nodes.label: Decision 016 — Strategy Master CSV per bucket (OR-semantics gate)
nodes.rationale: The PPTX said 'Excel header' but the user picked CSV-in-git: opens in Excel naturally, git-diffable, no binary churn. OR semantics match the natural reading of 'Trading Regime 1 or 2'; AND/weighted variants stay out of v1.

nodes.label: Decision 017 — Phase 1 soak restarts under the bucket structure
nodes.rationale: User chose 'restructure immediately, restart soak' — a cleaner single structure at the modest cost of ~5 days of soak data, avoiding two parallel runtime paths. Migration 0002 backfills old rows with the new bucket_id/strategy_name identifiers.

nodes.label: Decision 018 — Kelly insufficiency uses required margin, not notional
nodes.rationale: Decision 015's notional wording would cancel every leveraged trade, since notional > capital is the normal case for leveraged perps while margin stays tiny. The PPTX rule 'less balance than Kelly suggests, do not enter' reads as a margin check because margin is the actual cash at risk; the backtester must use the same check.

nodes.label: Decision 019 — One Delta India sub-account per crypto bucket
nodes.rationale: A perp exchange nets positions per symbol per account, so a shared account breaks bucket isolation three ways: leverage collision (per-symbol leverage makes the 5x/10x/25x/100x ladder unsatisfiable), cross-bucket interference and shared liquidation, and a reconciler that cannot attribute a netted position. A sub-account maps isolated capital 1:1 onto isolated account; only execution is per-account, market data stays shared.

nodes.label: Decision 020 — Regime retrain runs on the VM, not Railway
nodes.rationale: Retrain trains on Binance Futures klines and Binance geo-blocks Railway's region — every Railway retrain returned fetch_failed / n_bars=0 and models had silently gone stale since the 2026-06-14 manual seed. One daily systemd timer plus the job's --due mode preserves per-bucket cadence; inference was never affected because it reads bars from Delta.

nodes.label: Decision 021 — Exit engine, breaker enforcement, wallet mirror, dashboard auth
nodes.rationale: A full-project review found four gaps that made the pre-live soak unrepresentative: no exit path existed at all, breakers were defined but never invoked, bucket_state capital was never updated after the seed, and the dashboard had no auth. Exits run even for gated strategies because a gated strategy must still manage what it holds; a breaker trip halts then flattens, with recovery manual.

nodes.label: Decision 022 — Exchange-resident protective stop on every position
nodes.rationale: All prior exits are bot-driven, so if the bot or its VM is down nothing bounds the loss short of the exchange liquidation engine — the biggest remaining risk gap before go-live. stop_loss_pct is seeded at 0.5/leverage (50% of margin), well inside liquidation distance, and is a safety parameter rather than a strategy parameter so it needs no backtest_ref.

nodes.label: Decision 023 — Daily-anchored drawdown breaker
nodes.rationale: The breaker was daily in name only: it compared current unrealized PnL against current equity, so realized losses never counted (closing a loser reset it) and the denominator shrank with the losses — a day of repeated small realized losses could never trip it. Anchoring to a persisted start-of-day equity row makes it survive restarts (House Rule #3).

nodes.label: Decision 024 — Kill switch blocks risk-increasing actions only
nodes.rationale: An engaged kill switch previously skipped the bucket entirely, leaving a halted bucket holding positions completely unmanaged — no exit logic and no drawdown/liquidation watch. User chose option c: exits and breaker watch continue while killed, with acting gated and alerts dedup-capped so a persistent condition is watched silently.

nodes.label: Decision 025 — Kelly sizes on live equity; capital_inr is P&L baseline
nodes.rationale: The sizer computed against a static Rs50k while the wallet held ~Rs18k after testnet losses, producing oversized suggestions that mostly skipped as insufficient-margin and a dashboard P&L of -63.9% against capital the wallet never held. Sizing follows the account so the book scales with losses/gains; P&L follows a baseline of capital_inr plus recorded adjustments so deposits and withdrawals do not read as P&L.

nodes.label: Decision 026 — Multiple named scanner sets per bucket (CSV-linked)
nodes.rationale: One scanner.yaml per bucket forced every strategy to share one universe and one allocation config; the user wants a top-volume universe beside a momentum one, each Kelly-tuned separately. Option A (a CSV column, not scanner-owned subfolders) keeps the master CSV the single control sheet so re-pointing a strategy is a one-cell edit.

nodes.label: Decision 027 — Indian buckets size on a capped allocation
nodes.rationale: Crypto buckets are isolated by funding via Delta sub-accounts, but Dhan has no sub-accounts and its sandbox wallet is a fixed Rs10L that resets daily — unmodified Decision 025 would Kelly-size on 20x the intended bucket with no isolation from a future longterm-indian bucket. min(wallet, capital+adjustments) makes sandbox soak numbers read exactly like the real Rs50k bucket.

nodes.label: Decision 028 — swing-indian wide catastrophe stop (20%)
nodes.rationale: The Blasting Momentum backtest showed tight stops destroy the edge — day-1 noise knocks out eventual winners and exits belong to the strategy (Supertrend flip or 30-day cap). The broker stop is kept but set deliberately far outside normal strategy exits so it acts only as a crash net when bot or VM is down.

nodes.label: Decision 029 — Seventh bucket: intraday-indian
nodes.rationale: A holdout-validated NIFTY-100 gap-down reversal strategy is genuinely intraday (entries 09:30-10:30, square-off 15:15) and Decision 013's six buckets have no slot; a new bucket beat a second scanner set because forcing it under swing-indian would fight that bucket's 09:45 daily-prepare machinery for no saving. Ships disabled and is switched on by hand after review.

nodes.label: Decision 030 — intraday-indian: broad universe, MIS routing, shared capital, ledger P&L
nodes.rationale: Five user-chosen follow-ups: Rs50k capital (5 slots of Rs50k notional, since 5 slots of Rs1L is arithmetically impossible at 5x), an unvalidated broad Midcap150+Smallcap100 set run to generate its own evidence, a corrected circuit filter, per-order MIS routing sized to granted margin, and a shared capital budget with per-bucket ledger P&L.

nodes.label: Decision 031 — MIS-ineligible scrips fall back to 1x CNC
nodes.rationale: Decision 030(4) refused any CNC fallback, but the user chose to trade at 1x rather than skip. The hazard is a silent over-spend: a naive product swap re-sends the leveraged quantity as a cash order, demanding 4x the budgeted margin (Rs2L on a Rs50k bucket across 5 slots), so the fallback is always sized 1x, never upsizes, never places a stub, and records what was actually placed.

nodes.label: Decision 032 — swing-indian live on Midcap-150 1h mean reversion
nodes.rationale: A holdout-validated 1h mean-reversion strategy taken live with real money at quarter scale rather than staged on sandbox. Plan around the TRAIN grade (+24.7%, PF 2.31) not the crash-boosted holdout, because this is a convex buy-the-panic book; four sub-decisions cover quarter scale, retiring Blasting Momentum, resting the ATR stop on the exchange, and booking MTF interest.

nodes.label: Decision 033 — Session invariants and the agentic authority ceiling
nodes.rationale: Equity breakers ask 'has equity fallen off a cliff?' — the right question for a leveraged crypto sub-account and the wrong one for Indian equity, whose failure modes are procedural and happen at perfectly healthy equity: a missed 15:15 square-off, a position with no resting stop, a sizing over-commit, or a wedged bucket runner invisible to a process-level heartbeat.

nodes.label: buckets.yaml — single source of truth per bucket
nodes.rationale: Repo-root YAML holding capital, broker, leverage cap, enabled flag, account_ref, stop_loss_pct, entry_start/entry_end, fallback_product, carry_interest_apr and tick_interval_seconds per bucket.

nodes.label: bucket_state table (wallet-mirrored capital)
nodes.rationale: Postgres row tracking available_balance_inr and locked_margin_inr, synced from the sub-account wallet every reconciler sweep; 1:1 only because Decision 019 gives each bucket its own account, and it warns when an account is shared.

nodes.label: OR-semantics regime gate
nodes.rationale: A strategy trades if the current regime is in {trading_regime_1, trading_regime_2}, blanks ignored; both blank means regime-agnostic. Chosen because it matches the natural reading of 'Trading Regime 1 or 2'.

nodes.label: SizingDecision skip rules (INSUFFICIENT / NEGATIVE_EDGE / DEDUP)
nodes.rationale: All-or-nothing skips written to sizing_snapshot: SKIPPED_INSUFFICIENT when required margin exceeds available, SKIPPED_NEGATIVE_EDGE for mu <= 0 (long-only v1), SKIPPED_DEDUP on an open (bucket, strategy, symbol). Never size down — partial fills would ruin Kelly optimality.

nodes.label: stop_protection sweep (idempotent, self-healing)
nodes.rationale: Once per tick per sub-account after the bucket runners, it diffs exchange positions against resting stops: missing means place, size mismatch or trigger drift >0.5% means cancel and re-place, stop without a position means cancel. A sweep beats a per-order hook because it also protects positions predating the feature or opened manually.

nodes.label: Mark-price stop trigger snapped to tick_size
nodes.rationale: Triggering on mark price rather than last-traded avoids wicks on thin books; untriggered stops rest in Delta state 'pending', which is why get_open_orders queries states=open,pending.

nodes.label: daily_equity_anchor table
nodes.rationale: One unique row per (account_ref, UTC date) inserted on the first breaker pass of the day and read back afterwards so the anchor survives crashes. Known limits: mid-day deposits/withdrawals distort it, and a fully halted account only anchors after un-killing (the conservative choice).

nodes.label: allow_when_killed (reduce-only orders pass a killed switch)
nodes.rationale: Reduce-only orders — breaker flatten, strategy exits, protective stop placement — are risk-reducing and must be maintained even while a bucket is halted; risk-increasing orders never pass.

nodes.label: sizing_equity() — per-market Kelly capital base
nodes.rationale: Crypto uses the live sub-account wallet (available + locked) so profits compound automatically; Indian uses min(wallet_equity, capital_inr + adjustments) so a bucket never sizes on shared or simulated money it does not own.

nodes.label: capital_adjustments_inr (P&L baseline correction)
nodes.rationale: Stored in bucket_state.extra and written by scripts/record_capital_adjustment.py with an audit row, so a manual deposit or withdrawal does not read as P&L; --rebase zeroes P&L at the current wallet. Also the compounding lever for Indian buckets under Decision 027.

nodes.label: bucket_ledger_pnl (per-bucket P&L from Trade rows)
nodes.rationale: Indian buckets share one Dhan balance, so mirrored wallet equity double-counts P&L across them (latent while swing-indian was the only Indian bucket). Realized + unrealized from that bucket's own Trade rows replaces the mirror; crypto keeps the wallet mirror, which is correct under Decision 019.

nodes.label: Named scanner/allocator set (scanner_<name>.yaml + allocator_<name>.yaml)
nodes.rationale: Loaded at boot with fail-fast on a missing pair, one lazy scan per set per pipeline pass; named scans persist under strategy_id '<bucket_id>:<name>' to avoid colliding with the default scan's unique key. All sets share the bucket's one capital pool and sub-account.

nodes.label: committed_margin_inr running budget across scanner sets
nodes.rationale: size_positions ran once per strategy each sizing against full bucket capital, so two sets at aggregate_cap 1.00 could each claim 100% (200% of the bucket) in one tick. The runner now threads a running committed margin, capped at min(wallet, capital); slots are first-come-first-served in sorted filename order so the validated set claims ahead of the broad one.

nodes.label: OrderRequest.fallback_max_size (1x-sized product fallback)
nodes.rationale: The quantity affordable with no leverage (margin_budget / price, floored), computed by BucketRunner._one_x_size, applied as min(size, cap) on any leveraged-product rejection. Opt-in per bucket via fallback_product; never upsizes, never sends a sub-1-share stub, and OrderResult.size writes the clamped quantity back to Trade.quantity because ownership scoping, P&L and stop sizing all read that column.

nodes.label: Circuit filter: F&O underlying OR hard band >= 20%
nodes.rationale: The obvious 'hard band >= 20%' filter is actively wrong: only 2 of 99 NIFTY-100 names have one, because 97 are F&O underlyings with a dynamic band, so a naive width filter would reject the validated universe outright. The real hazard is non-F&O narrow-band scrips that can lock intraday and strand a long until auto square-off; 82 of the 100 smallcaps are non-F&O, a residual risk the validation does not cover.

nodes.label: MIS sizing to granted margin (required_margin then max_leverage then 1x)
nodes.rationale: leverage_max: 5 is a risk CEILING, not a target — measured medians are 4.44x NIFTY-100, 3.79x Midcap150, 3.06x Smallcap100 and not one name reaches 5x, so flat-5x sizing would over-order on effectively every trade and collect an RMS rejection. Sources in order of authority: the venue's margin calculator, then the scrip master figure capped at the bucket ceiling, then 1x. Expect return on margin proportionally below the backtest's 5x assumption.

nodes.label: Per-symbol stop_distances override (tighten-only)
nodes.rationale: The strategy emits a rupee distance in EntryCandidate.hint, BucketRunner stamps it on Trade.extra via place_order(extra_payload=...), and plan_stop_protection reads it back. A distance WIDER than the bucket's percent net is refused and logged, so the configured worst case holds no matter what the ATR read does; buckets supplying no distance behave exactly as before.

nodes.label: carry_interest_apr (bot books MTF funding cost)
nodes.rationale: The backtest omits Dhan's ~4% funding cost, so the reconciler subtracts (notional - margin) x rate x days/365 from realized P&L on each round-trip close — funded portion only, so the 1x CNC fallback pays nothing. Reporting a P&L the strategy never earned would corrupt every downstream read.

nodes.label: Midcap-150 1h mean reversion strategy
nodes.rationale: A FRESH downward cross of dist = (close/ema20 - 1) x 100 below -6.5% goes long at the next bar's open, so a stuck-stretched name does not re-fire. Exits: 1h close >= EMA20 (primary), a 3.5 x daily-ATR14 stop, or 20 trading days. Long-only, <=5 new entries/day, one position per symbol, on NIFTY-Midcap-150 intersect NSE F&O (94 names).

nodes.label: Blasting Momentum made inert (_blasting_momentum.py)
nodes.rationale: Enabling the bucket would have armed an order path that never ran outside the Dhan sandbox, so the file gets a leading underscore (loader skips it) and no strategy_master.csv row. Knock-on effects: the default scanner set becomes equity_meanrev_1h so the nightly dhan-prepare timer no longer sweeps 4,600 names, and regime.yaml is disabled because the bull/neutral gate cut in-sample net from +30.7% to +2-9% by removing the crash-rebound trades that ARE the edge.

nodes.label: BucketRunner paces at the bucket's fastest timeframe
nodes.rationale: Pacing off the regime model's timeframe would let a 1d model delay every 1h signal by up to 15 minutes, so pacing follows the fastest strategy timeframe with an explicit tick_interval_seconds: 60 override; run_meanrev_scan caches per 1h bin so a 60s loop re-fetches ~190 calls per bin rather than per minute.

nodes.label: last_complete_bar_key and the 15:15-15:30 stub bin
nodes.rationale: A signal is actionable only while its bin is the most recently completed one — the live equivalent of the backtest's 'fill at the next bar's open' (House Rule 9). A 1h NSE session has 7 bins with a 15-minute last one, a real signal bar in the backtest (3 of 214 trades), so the key keeps naming it until the next session's first bin closes.

nodes.label: meanrev_1h_parity.py — 208/214 trade reproduction
nodes.rationale: Replays the port over the same cached 15m/1D CSVs on three axes (fresh cross on the same bin, dist within 0.15pp, ATR stop within 0.1%). The six misses are all the EMA20 warm-up guard at a data boundary and are all winners, so the port is conservative rather than broken.

nodes.label: NIFTY-100 gap-down reversal (intraday-indian)
nodes.rationale: Entries 09:30-10:30, square-off 15:15, no overnight risk. Holdout grade (frozen, includes the Apr-2025 crash): 35 trades, +13.3% on deployed margin, win 51%, PF 1.68, maxDD 9.2% — not the full-period +36.6%. Flow is ~0.8 trades/week; zero-signal days are normal and must not be fixed by loosening filters.

nodes.label: Regime gate OFF for intraday-indian
nodes.rationale: The strategy fades panic — its signals are generated BY bearish tape and the frozen holdout that earned +13.3% contains the April-2025 crash, so a bull/neutral gate would mute it exactly when it works. A deliberate departure from Decision 014, revisit only with a backtest showing a gate helps.

nodes.label: Live corporate-action guard (intraday vs adjusted daily prev-close)
nodes.rationale: The engine's scale-invariant check needs TODAY's daily bar, which Dhan does not publish until well after the close (the 2026-07-14 STALE-CLOSE bug), so it is unusable at 09:30. Live compares the intraday gap against the same gap on the adjusted daily prev-close; the accepted cost is skipping a name when replaying a date before a corporate action (VEDL 2025-08-26). The within-series-ratio alternative is worse because the 5m series misses the closing auction.

nodes.label: Authority ladder (L0 notice / L1-L2 halt / L3 flatten)
nodes.rationale: Invariants and any future supervisor agent are capped at HALT; only a deterministic breaker may FLATTEN. This is what keeps House Rule #1 intact: an invariant is an assertion about PROCESS, not a view on the market, and engaging a kill switch is strictly risk-reducing and reversible while closing a position is a trading decision.

nodes.label: Tier 1 session_invariants.py (observe-only)
nodes.rationale: Six checks per 60s tick per account, run AFTER the stop sweep so 'no stop' means the sweep failed rather than has not run: squareoff, stop_coverage (2 consecutive ticks), notional_ceiling, reject_rate, bucket_liveness, foreign_positions (never acted on — that is the user's book). Ships with session_invariants_enforcing=false because an untested check that can halt a live bucket on its first false positive is a worse trade than a Telegram message; sustain streaks keep counting so flipping the flag needs no warm-up.

nodes.label: effective_holdings — ledger intersected with exchange positions
nodes.rationale: The Trade ledger alone goes stale when something closes a position without writing a SELL row (Dhan's own MIS auto-square-off does exactly that, leaving a phantom holding that fails the square-off invariant forever); exchange positions alone cannot tell the bot's rows from the user's on the shared Dhan account. Intersecting two independent sources fixes both.

nodes.label: Notional ceiling applies to INR-equity buckets only
nodes.rationale: Delta positions are contract-denominated and USD-priced, so qty x entry_price is neither a base-unit size nor rupees; BucketWatch.notional_budget_inr=None skips the check.

nodes.label: Tier 2 intraday supervisor agent (designed, not built)
nodes.rationale: An LLM at ~6 fixed IST checkpoints reading a Postgres-only snapshot, catching what thresholds cannot: entry rate far off the backtest baseline, every fill at its bar's extreme, a symbol cycling in and out, a sizing_snapshot skip reason spiking. Authority capped at L1 halt, then page. Must never call the Dhan API, because a second session evicts the bot's token — a broker-polling monitor would cause the outage it exists to detect.

nodes.label: Tier 3 EOD session report (src/reporting/eod.py)
nodes.rationale: Runs 15:45 IST, after the 15:15 square-off and 15:30 close, so what is still open genuinely IS carried overnight. The nightly Parquet export is an archive, not a report — this answers what each bucket made, WHICH SIGNALS DID NOT TRADE AND WHY (sizing_snapshot has held that record since Decision 026 and nothing had ever read it back), what tripped, and whether the live edge tracks the backtest. A quiet day says so plainly, because a report that looks broken on a normal day is one you stop reading.

nodes.label: session_report table and /journal route
nodes.rationale: Postgres is the store because the Railway scheduler container is ephemeral and holds no git credentials; one UPSERTed row per date. export_journal.py materialises rows into docs/journal/*.md with opt-in --commit, safe on the VM because deploy.sh's RESTART_PATHS excludes docs/. The dashboard renders with a ~60-line local subset renderer over a closed grammar and escapes BEFORE it formats, so a broker message with angle brackets cannot inject markup.

nodes.label: signal_price / decision_price / avg_fill_price triple
nodes.rationale: What the strategy SAW is not something the exchange knows and is unrecoverable unless recorded at decision time, so every unrecorded day was live evidence permanently lost. Splitting the gap into decision lag (fix: scan latency / tick cadence) and execution cost (fix: spread, impact, order type) says WHICH one to go fix; positive is always a cost on both sides so entries and exits do not cancel into a comforting zero. Exits carry no signal_price because select_exits returns bare symbols.

nodes.label: backtest_baseline in allocator.yaml
nodes.rationale: Lives beside backtest_ref and pooled mu/sigma so House Rule 7 holds; purely descriptive and the sizer never reads it. win_rate is deliberately blank for both live buckets because a guessed baseline is worse than none. PF and win rate are scale-invariant, which makes a live rupee figure comparable to an unlevered backtest figure; a PF with no losing round-trip is reported as UNDEFINED, not infinite, and below 20 closed round-trips the section leads with a 'too early to read' banner.

nodes.label: Watchdogs run off the Mumbai VM
nodes.rationale: A dead VM must not be able to silence its own watchdog — the same reasoning that put the heartbeat watch on Railway. Decision 020's Binance geo-block does not apply because neither tier touches Binance.

nodes.label: Fixed USD/INR = 85 (no live FX feed)
nodes.rationale: User decision recorded under Decision 024, superseding the Phase 1c 'live FX' item: fx_inr_per_usd: 85.0 in each bucket's allocator.yaml is the single source and the frankfurter.app fetch was removed the same day. Live contract sizes from /v2/products are unaffected.

nodes.label: OrderManager transport-error recovery by client_order_id
nodes.rationale: Query the exchange by client_order_id before marking a trade REJECTED so a response timeout cannot double-fire next tick (House Rule #2). Landed the same session: set_leverage failure now aborts placement instead of warn-and-continue, and regime inference/training drop the in-progress candle.
